title: 'Flamingo Revolution' Mounts Direct Threat to Albania's Edi Rama
content:
What began as a localized environmental campaign against a luxury resort development backed by Jared Kushner has hardened into a 100-day siege of Albania’s political center, mounting the most formidable challenge in years to the government of Prime Minister Edi Rama.

Demonstrators marched along Tirana’s main thoroughfares, rallying near local high schools to mobilize students into the movement, dubbed by organizers as the “Flamingo Revolution” as flamingos inhabit the protected Vjosa-Narta wetland ecosystem where the resort was supposed to be built. Chanting “Rama, resign” and “Your time is up,” protesters confronted security forces in the latest escalation of a campaign that has repeatedly paralyzed parts of the capital.

The unrest originally erupted over government plans to allow Kushner’s firm, Affinity Partners, to construct high-end tourism facilities on the uninhabited Sazan Island and within the protected Vjosa-Narta wetland along the Adriatic coast. While Rama framed the investment as a key catalyst for tourism and European Union integration, environmentalists fiercely opposed the privatization of pristine reserves.

title: Papa Johns, Propaganda and Putin: How a MAGA Influencer With Ties to Russia Became Trump’s Arctic Adviser
content:
For more than 40 years, the U.S. Arctic Research Commission has advised Congress and the president on what to study in the frigid and dynamic far north, from the environment to military security. It’s typically done so without making waves, led by people well-versed in science and public policy.

That was until December, when President Donald Trump appointed a Texas venture capitalist and MAGA influencer with no formal background in science as the commission’s chair. Since then, Thomas Dans has traveled the globe generating headlines. Serving as the administration’s main voice on the Arctic, he’s advanced some of the president’s wildest ambitions, like a takeover of Greenland, and rankled NATO allies in the process.

Yet as Dans holds forth in the U.S. and abroad, it’s not always clear where the administration’s agenda ends and his own begins.

He has repeatedly said, for example, that the U.S. needs more icebreakers, ships that Trump has long viewed as critical to dominating the Arctic. In doing so, Dans has championed one shipbuilder in particular — Damen Shipyards, a Dutch company with which he had a business relationship.

title: Europe’s e-waste is a valuable resource – let’s not throw it away
content:
Throwing something away that is urgently needed, expensive and difficult to source sounds crazy. Yet out of the 60 metals contained in old electronic devices like phones, screens or washing machines, only a few get recycled. That includes precious metals like gold or silver and some other metals like aluminium or copper. The rest are effectively single-use metals, used once then lost during collection or through incineration.

Metals are mined from ore and refined by using a lot of energy and resources as part of complex global supply chains. Think of the diesel needed to power the huge trucks in the mine, the chemicals needed to extract the metals from the ores or the pollution from intense furnaces.

By throwing away metal-rich electronics and not recovering these precious resources, we lose all the effort we put into getting the metals out of the ground. Yet these metals are urgently needed for green technologies such as wind turbines and heat pumps, as well as for conventional industries including car manufacturing, aerospace or the production of machinery. At the same time, most of them are not physically accessible for mining within Europe.

title: HS: Palloliitto kompuroi Suomelle nootin Ukrainasta
content:
Ukrainan suurlähetystö on lähettänyt diplomaattisen nootin Suomen ulkoministeriölle Huuhkajien kotipelistä Valko-Venäjää vastaan, Helsingin Sanomat uutisoi tiistaina.

Suomi isännöi Valko-Venäjää jalkapallon Kansojen liigassa 29. syyskuuta Olympiastadionilla Helsingissä. Ukrainan Suomen-suurlähettiläs Myhailo Vydoinyk sanoi Helsingin Sanomille toivovansa, että Palloliitto muuttaisi vielä päätöstään ja siirtäisi ottelun Suomen rajojen ulkopuolelle.

PALLOLIITTO on kirjaimellisesti pallotellut otteluasiaa jo pitkään. Maaliskuussa liitto päätti, ettei ottelua pelata Suomessa.

Toukokuussa liitto ilmoitti, että ottelu pelataan sittenkin Helsingissä. Liitto perusteli alkuperäisen päätöksensä pyörtämistä muun muassa Kansainvälisen olympiakomitean KOK:n muuttuneella linjauksella, kansainvälisillä kokemuksilla, urheilullisella oikeudenmukaisuudella ja pelaajien sekä kannattajien halulla.

Palloliitto on ilmoittanut, että ottelun lipunmyynnin nettotuotot menevät ukrainalaisten tukemiseen. HS:n mukaan otteluun oli myyty maanantaihin mennessä vain 5 000 pääsylippua.

LIITON TOIMINTA kansainvälisen kattojärjestö Fifan johdon tukemisessa suututti kesällä kotimaisia jalkapallofaneja.

title: Hanna Holopainen: Tyttöjen potentiaali luonnontieteellisillä aloilla on tunnistettava
content:
Suomalaisnuoret pärjäävät luonnontieteissä edelleen kansainvälisesti hyvin, mutta osaamisen pitkän aikavälin kehitys on laskeva. Vihreiden kansanedustaja Hanna Holopainen pitää suuntaa huolestuttavana. Hän nostaa esiin erityisesti tyttöjen osaamisen ja myöhempien koulutus- ja uravalintojen välisen ristiriidan.

Myös oppilaiden väliset osaamiserot koulujen sisällä ovat Suomessa kasvaneet selvästi OECD-maiden keskiarvoa suuremmiksi.

Tuoreessa PISA 2025 -tutkimuksessa suomalaisnuorten luonnontieteiden keskiarvo oli 504 pistettä, kun OECD-maiden keskiarvo oli 482. Suomi menestyi Pohjoismaista parhaiten. Vuonna 2022 Suomen pistemäärä oli 511, mutta ero uusimpaan tulokseen ei ole tilastollisesti merkitsevä. Pidemmällä aikavälillä luonnontieteiden osaamisen lasku on kuitenkin selvä.

”Suomi sijoittui luonnontieteissä edelleen Pohjoismaista parhaiten, mutta kehityssuunta on silti huolestuttava. Luonnontieteiden vankka osaaminen on ollut monen elinkeinoelämän sektorin kivijalka, eikä Suomella ole varaa menettää sitä. Luonnontieteiden osaamisen merkitys vain korostuu ilmastokriisin ja luontokadon torjunnan osalta”, Holopainen sanoo.

title: Growing from Wiki Club to Becoming a Community Towards the Future
content:
Reflections on the Wikimedia Malaysia 2026 Strategic Direction Conference

After discovering the Wikimedia platform, I began my journey of promoting and preserving my community’s language, Kadazandusun, through my participation in Wiki Club Kent. The club gave me an opportunity to learn more about the Wikimedia movement and to contribute to the world of free knowledge.

Today, that journey continues with the same mission. Although my time as a student and as a Wiki Club member has come to an end, my passion for contributing remains. I hope to take the Kadazandusun language further into the world as part of this community.

On 30th August 2026, I had the opportunity to participate in the Malaysian Wikimedia Strategy Summit 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, which brought together Wikimedians and community leaders from diverse backgrounds across Malaysia. For me, this was more than just a conference. It was a space for us to pause, reflect on the journey we have taken so far, and envision where the Malaysian Wikimedia community wants to go next.

title: ‘I created my mom and talk to her’: AI ghosts and deathslop are changing the way we mourn
content:
The rise of AI-generated tributes and bots for ‘talking’ to the dead has experts concerned more people will grieve in isolation

Tributes rolled in after the death of Dolly Parton last month. Jack White performed Jolene at a London gig. Kesha sang Old Flames (Can’t Hold a Candle to You), a single her mother wrote for the country music titan. Even Pitbull stopped his Madison Square Garden show to memorialize Parton and all the other “powerful women” in the crowd. But one of the strangest – and most viral – eulogies did not come from a celebrity. It did not even come from a person.

Run Jolene, at just under five minutes, is an earworm of a country song, containing all the cliches of the genre: twangy singer, banjo licks, corny lyrics. Those lyrics concern Jolene, the fictional romantic rival made infamous by Parton. “Somebody better warn Jolene / Dolly’s coming through those gates,” the voice croons. “Run Jolene / Girl you better move your feet.”

title: Elevernas utbildningsvägar börjar skilja sig åt redan under de första åren i den grundläggande utbildningen
content:
Elevens kunnande i början av den grundläggande utbildningen har ett starkt samband med senare utbildningsval. I en longitudinell studie vid Nationella centret för utbildningsutvärdering (NCU) visade sig elevernas relativa placering i kunskapsgrupper vara relativt bestående från årskurs 3 till slutet av den grundläggande utbildningen. Även föräldrarnas socioekonomiska ställning hade ett samband med de ungas utbildningsvägar.

I studien följdes samma elevers kunnande under den grundläggande utbildningen åren 2005–2012. År 2025 kompletterades materialet med Statistikcentralens registeruppgifter, som användes för att granska deltagarnas utbildning och socioekonomiska ställning i ung vuxen ålder. Det longitudinella materialet från tiden i den grundläggande utbildningen omfattade 3 502 elever. I de utbildnings- och arbetsmarknadsanalyser som baserade sig på registeruppgifter ingick 2 918 personer.

title: German Car Crisis: A Defense Bonanza?
content:
Volkswagen, the world’s second-largest auto manufacturer, is slashing 100,000 jobs. Auto suppliers Bosch and ZF are cutting tens of thousands more, putting at risk a combined 350,000 jobs across the continent. 

But behind the grim news, there’s hope: Europe’s struggling automakers are diversifying into defense manufacturing. Israel’s Rafael signed a letter of intent to take over Volkswagen’s 2,300-worker Osnabrück factory. It plans to build Iron Dome launchers, generators and trucks. Renault has cleared a 5,000-square-meter hall to assemble Chorus strike drones. Auto supplier Schaeffler is selling electronics parts to German drone maker Helsing. 

Europe’s defense and car industries make natural partners. They require similar skills. One is growing. The other is declining, bloodied by Chinese competition and the transition to electric vehicles. By working together, the two can offset the pain and increase the continent’s security — provided they can overcome several obstacles.

title: OpenAI: AI capabilities are in a ‘different place’ and require urgency
content:
President Donald Trump called AI concerns a “hoax.” One of the country’s leading AI companies said Tuesday it’s hoping Washington will still act.

OpenAI, which this weekend called for federal safety measures alongside its rival Anthropic, said it spent the beginning of the week meeting with members of both parties to discuss legislation that would rein in AI developers as warnings of impending doom, job loss and massive cyberattacks become increasingly prevalent.

Models are developing at breakneck speed and agents are acting in ways that engineers are struggling to predict or control. Even as there have long been calls for regulation, recent hacks of companies such as Hugging Face have engendered fresh waves of concern that the technology is reaching a point in which it is capable of causing serious harm.

“We have certainly conveyed that really over the last month that capabilities are in a different place, and as a result of those capabilities being in a different place, we do feel like there needs to be an urgency to this,” Chris Lehane, OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer, said the company told the White House.

title: Algeria: Threats to resume executions after 30 years severe blow to human rights
content: Algeria’s authorities must immediately abandon any plans to expand the scope of the death penalty or resume executions after more than three decades without carrying one out, said Amnesty International as the government examines amendments to the penal code that would broaden the use of the death penalty. The organization calls on Algeria’s authorities to immediately establish an official moratorium as a first step towards fully abolishing the death penalty. It also urges the authorities to adopt a human-rights centred response to the recent devastating wildfires, including by ensuring effective investigations into all factors that led to the tragic loss of life and accountability without resort to the death penalty.

title: Three Baha’i Citizens Arrested in Shiraz
content:
According to HRANA, three Baha’i citizens have been arrested in Shiraz.

HRANA has confirmed the identities of these individuals as Sarina Zaeri, 20, Barbad Sepehri, 21, and Arshia Jaberi, 19.

These citizens were arrested by security forces at their homes yesterday. Following their arrests, the Baha’i citizens were transferred to an undisclosed location.

As of the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for their arrests, their place of detention, or the charges brought against them.

Over the past decade, Iran’s Baha’i community has faced more security and judicial actions than any other religious minority in the country. A review of HRA’s annual reports shows that, during the previous calendar year, an average of 62.41% of reports concerning religious minorities involved violations of the civil rights of Baha’is.

title: Vučić Dissolves Parliament: Serbia Heads to Snap Election
content:
The decision comes after nearly two years of mass protests that erupted following the disaster at Novi Sad railway station in November 2024, when a concrete canopy collapsed, killing 16 people and igniting a broader anti-corruption and anti-authoritarian movement.

President Aleksandar Vučić, who has dominated Serbian politics since 2012 — first as prime minister and later as president — has announced that if his coalition wins the election, he will take over as head of government.

The decision to dissolve parliament was preceded by an announcement from the government made by Prime Minister Đuro Macut on September 7. Two days later, Vučić personally signed both documents.

The disaster at Novi Sad railway station unleashed a wave of protests that has continued ever since. From the outset, demonstrators demanded a transparent investigation and punishment for those responsible for the deaths of 16 people. In the spring of 2025, student blockades joined the movement, while the list of demands expanded to include calls for an early election.

title: A Digital Fly Brain Has Taken Over the Internet
content:
A digital fly brain has been trading bitcoin, parallel parking, exploring bisexuality, cutting doner kebab, playing games—including Minecraft, Doom, and Beat Saber—and generally lighting up social media timelines since it was released earlier this month.

The simulated brain, known as a connectome, is a complete map of more than 166,000 neurons that make up the nervous system of an adult male Drosophila fruit fly. Developed by HHMI Janelia Research Campus in partnership with Google Research, the connectome (dubbed MaleCNS v1.0) was unveiled earlier this month, following the release of the first adult female fruit fly connectome in 2024.

“We present the first finished connectome of an entire male Drosophila central nervous system, encompassing the central brain, optic lobes (analogous to mammalian retina) and the ventral nerve cord (analogous to the spinal cord),” the team announced in a press release on September 3. “Together with existing female connectomes, this resource enables the first comprehensive, synaptic-resolution comparison across sexes of an adult animal with complex anatomy and behaviors.”

title: The Son of Ljubljana’s Mayor Granted Serbian Citizenship in “National Interest”
content:
Serbian authorities granted citizenship to the son of Ljubljana’s mayor under a discreet "national interest" provision while declining to publicise the justification of its decision. The move coincides with high-value real estate purchases in the Slovenian capital by a key ally of the Serbian president, a businessman at whose Belgrade villa the mayor's son registered his official residence.

According to official records obtained by investigative news outlets Oštro and KRIK, Jure Janković - son of long-serving Ljubljana Mayor Zoran Janković - was naturalized as a Serbian citizen in November 2024. Land registry documents show that the younger Janković registered his Belgrade address at a luxury villa owned by Nikola Petrović, a powerful energy executive known widely as the "best man" and close confidant of Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić.

title: Underage Players, Predatory Moneylenders: 7 Findings From Our Dominican Baseball Investigation
content:
Baseball is everywhere in the Dominican Republic, which sends a disproportionate number of players to the American major and minor leagues, including Hall of Famers like Pedro Martínez and Adrian Beltré. Playing fields and training academies dot the country in villages where players who’ve made the leap to the pros are immortalized in murals.

For nearly half a century, the Dominican Republic has sent more players to the majors than any country outside the United States. The nation, which has a population roughly that of Ohio’s, had 144 players reach the major leagues last year. That’s about 10% of the league.

The Dominican baseball factory is a volume business, with teams paying signing bonuses to about 450 prospects each year. Fewer than 10% of those young players will ever see a single pitch in the majors, but in a country as impoverished as the Dominican Republic those bonuses — worth several times the country’s average annual income — could be life-changing for the players and their families. Yet Major League Baseball has long allowed a corrosive system to fester that rigs the game against young players in favor of opportunistic trainers and predatory moneylenders.

title: Suomi toimittaa Ukrainaan puolustustarvikeapua 290 miljoonalla eurolla
content:
Suomi lähettää 290 miljoonan euron arvoisen puolustustarvikeapupaketin Ukrainalle. Asiasta kertoi tiistaina puolustusministeriö. Kyseessä on 34. Suomen Ukrainalle lähettämä puolustusmateriaalipaketti.

Suomi on toimittanut Ukrainaan puolustusmateriaalia nyt yhteensä 3,6 miljardin euron arvosta. Nyt lähetettävä tukipaketti on puolustusministeriön mukaan rahalliselta arvoltaan toiseksi suurin Suomen myöntämistä paketeista.

Paketti sisältää etenkin Ukrainan kiireellisesti pyytämiä materiaaleja. Puolustusministeriö ei kuitenkaan avaa tarkemmin apupaketin sisältöä, aikataulua tai toimitustapaa muun muassa avun turvallisen perillemenon takaamiseksi.

Presidentti päätti tukipaketin lähettämisestä valtioneuvoston esityksestä tiistaina.

title: Women, the Sundanese Language, and Wikimedia Projects
content:
In our daily life, there are things we do not notice while they are still around us. A mother tongue can be one of them. We grow up hearing it at home, in conversations with family,  jokes exchanged between neighbours, or stories told before bedtime. We rarely stop to think about how many of our memories are carried by the words we inherit. However, when those words begin to disappear, we do realize that a language is never simply a collection of vocabulary, It is a way of remembering who we are.

I am a Sundanese woman, and Sundanese is part of the memory. 

For me, the question of whether the Sundanese language will continue to live is not merely a linguistic question. It is a deeply personal one. It is connected to the kind of world we will leave behind for the generations that come after us. Will they still be able to read old expressions, understand the stories told by their grandparents, recognize the names of plants and places in their own language? Or they simply have the freedom to say, “This is my language.”

content:
Vantaan Fazerilan ratikkapysäkin taiteilijaksi on valittu kuvanveistäjä Piia Hiltunen. Hänen lisäkseen rinnakkaiseen luonnostilaukseen kutsuttiin taiteilijat Anna Hyrkkänen, Noora Schroderus ja Jiri Geller. Hiltusen ehdotus etenee seuraavaksi toteutussuunnitteluun ja tulee valmistuessaan osaksi Fazerilan kehittyvää kaupunginosaa. Pysäkkialueelle toteutettava teos tulee osaksi Vantaan taidemuseo Artsin julkisen taiteen kokoelmaa.

Hiltusen ehdotuksessa veistokselliset ja leikkisät elementit yhdistyvät pysäkkikatokseen ja sen viherkattoon. Ehdotus on tarinallinen, lämminhenkinen ja omintakeinen. Teosluonnoksessa viherkatto on otettu osaksi taidekokonaisuutta ja sen lajisto viittaa Fazerilan alueen historiaan viljelymaana. Pronssinen veistosaihe ja kasvillisuus yhdessä muodostavat ajatuksia herättävän kokonaisuuden. Teosehdotuksessa on monia tasoja ja se antaa tilaa ratikkaa odottavan mielikuvitukselle.

– Teos muistuttaa meitä luonnon merkityksestä osana kehittyvää kaupunkiympäristöä, julkisen taiteen kuraattori Heli Lukkarinen sanoo.

Fazerilan pysäkki sijoittuu alueelle, joka muuttuu tulevina vuosina merkittävästi. Ratikan varteen Fazerila–Santamalmiin suunnitellaan uutta monipuolista asuin- ja työpaikka-aluetta lähipalveluineen. Ratikka kytkee alueen tiiviimmin osaksi muuta Vantaata ja tukee kestävän, joukkoliikenteeseen tukeutuvan kaupunginosan rakentumista. Uusi taideteos tekee ratikkapysäkistä tunnistettavan paikan jo alueen rakentumisen alkuvaiheessa ja tuo julkisen taiteen näkyväksi osaksi uudistuvaa kaupunkiympäristöä.

title: EU countries to discuss AI rules as Trump calls safety warnings a ‘hoax’
content:
Government officials from across the European Union will gather in Brussels on Thursday to discuss how to set global rules to counter the threat from new AI models, according to two EU diplomats and a draft agenda seen by POLITICO.

The European Commission will give “updates on EU and international AI policy” and give a “technical briefing on recent AI incidents” during a gathering of the Artificial Intelligence Board, which comprises of representatives from every EU member country and regularly convenes to monitor progress on the bloc’s Artificial Intelligence Act.

This week’s gathering follows a series of calls to slow down AI development by top company leaders such as Anthropic’s Dario Amodei and OpenAI’s Sam Altman. U.S. President Donald Trump immediately rebuffed the calls, calling the AI safety warnings a “hoax” and arguing that slowing down would give China the momentum in AI.

The European discussions on global cooperation will focus on work done at the G7, the G20 and the United Nations, one of the diplomats said.

Last Friday, the European Commission’s top tech official, Executive Vice President for Tech Sovereignty Henna Virkkunen, called for global AI rules and cooperation.

title: “They told us to leave and never to come back” – The Malian survivors of the conflict who have been forced into exile by armed groups
content:
Over the past decade, the conflict in Mali between the armed forces and their allies and various non-state armed groups has forced hundreds of thousands of people to flee their country, including to Mauritania.

Certain armed groups, in particular the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (GSIM), also known as Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM), and the Islamic State – Sahel province (ISSP), violate the right to religious freedom, and plunder civilians’ goods and resources. They are also driving people out of their villages, particularly in the Ségou, Timbuktu, and Mopti regions.

In July 2026, 290,000 Malian refugees were registered by the UNHCR in the wilaya [region] of Hodh Ech-Chargui, in southeastern Mauritania, near the Malian border.

Amnesty International visited them in 2025 and 2026 as part of a research about abuses committed by the parties to the conflict in Mali.

Husseini* was a herder in Mali. He left the Ségou region in October 2024 with members of his family and now lives in the hamlet of Kleiva, in Mauritania.

title: Jasem Savaedi Arrested by Security Forces in Hamidiyeh
content:
According to HRANA, Jasem Savaedi (Saedi) has been arrested.

According to information received by HRANA, Mr. Savaedi was arrested today, Monday, September 14, 2026, by forces from the Ahvaz Intelligence Department.

As of the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for his arrest, the charges against him, or his place of detention.

Jasem Savaedi was previously arrested in February 2012 along with several others. They were tried by the Ahvaz Revolutionary Court on charges including “enmity against God” (moharebeh) and “corruption on earth” (efsad-e fel-arz). Mr. Savaedi was ultimately sentenced to 15 years in prison and, after serving approximately 11 years, was conditionally released from prison in January 2023.

Hassan Abyat, one of Mr. Savaedi’s co-defendants, was sentenced to death on the charge of “enmity against God” (moharebeh). His sentence was carried out at dawn on February 20, 2023, in Sepidar Prison in Ahvaz.

Jasem Savaedi (Saedi), aged approximately 42, is a resident of Hamidiyeh, Khuzestan province.

title: There’s a 100% Chance AI Agents Are Already Ruining the Internet
content:
For the last week, much of society has been focused on the idea that there’s a “more than 10 percent chance” AI could kill all humans within the next decade. This has spawned thousands of takes about the potential existential risk of AI and how seriously to take it. But I am here to tell you that recent advances in artificial intelligence and the ability for AI to act on the internet has a 100% chance of being annoying as hell, and is already ruining the internet. 

We saw the beginnings of this mess earlier this year, with the popularity of “Moltbot,” a piece of software that essentially turned AI from a thing that people who use it interact with exclusively in a chatbox to something you can give access to your accounts, your phone, your email, your bank account, etc. Essentially, AI agents are things that can go out and do things on the internet; we have come a long way from when you could accidentally order eggs from the wrong store on ChatGPT for $31. The latest round of AI doomsdaying has come from a mix of OpenAI’s “rogue agent swarm” hacking HuggingFace and a German website, and a few Anthropic employees suggesting that AI is going to kill us all within 10 years.

title: Citing Trump Crypto Fortune, US Democrats Try to Derail Bill to Regulate Digital Assets
content:
Congressional Democrats are using the sudden surge in crypto wealth accumulated by U.S. President Donald Trump as a rallying cry to defeat legislation that would create a new regulatory landscape for the digital currency industry.

The Senate is scheduled to take a procedural vote Tuesday on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, which if passed by both legislative chambers would set new rules to govern the growing crypto sector. The procedural vote is needed for the Senate to debate the measure.

In a bid to peel off some Democrats, Republican Party leaders in Congress over the weekend incorporated ethics provisions that would prevent any U.S. president or other government officials from issuing digital assets.

“It purports to prevent conflicts of interest and corruption by the president of the United States. It is a charade. It is a sham. It should prompt a no vote by every member of the United States Senate,” said Sen. Richard Blumenthal, a Connecticut Democrat.

title: Liettuassa ammuttiin alas maan ilmatilaan lentänyt drooni
content:
Sotilasliitto Naton hävittäjät ovat ampuneet droonin alas Liettuan ilmatilassa, kertoo Liettuan presidentti Gitanas Nauseda.

Presidentti kertoi viestipalvelu X:ssä puolenyön jälkeen, että Naton hävittäjät olivat tuhonneet Liettuan ilmatilaan tulleen droonin.

Liettuan kriisinhallintakeskus kertoo Liettuan yleisradioyhtiö LRT:lle, että drooni ammuttiin alas maan eteläosassa lähellä Kaunasin kaupunkia puolenyön jälkeen. Alustavan arvion mukaan drooni tuli Liettuan ilmatilaan todennäköisesti Valko-Venäjältä, mutta sen alkuperää ei ole vahvistettu.

Droonista annettiin varoitus pääkaupunki Vilnaan ja sitä ympäröivälle alueelle. Henkilövahinkoja tai aineellisia vahinkoja ei tiettävästi aiheutunut.

Presidentti Nauseda kiittää Naton henkilöstöä nopeasta toiminnasta.

- Venäjän voimistaessa aggressiotaan Ukrainaa vastaan tällainen valmius on alueellemme elintärkeää. Liettua puolustaa ilmatilaansa yhdessä Nato-liittolaistensa kanssa, presidentti kommentoi.

Sunnuntaina Liettuassa annettiin lyhyehkö ilmauhkahälytys, jonka kuitenkin aiheutti droonin sijaan lintuparvi.

title: ‘We were bored of traditional fantasy cliches’: inside Playground Games’ 10-year effort to revive Fable
content:
The distinctively British RPG is returning courtesy of the makers of Forza Horizon – with comedy talent such as Richard Ayoade and Natasia Demetriou voicing sweary characters. We had our first play and spoke to its developer

When Playground Games was founded in 2010, its objective was straightforward: to make the best cars in video games. Operating out of an unassuming white building in Leamington Spa, the studio sought to challenge Gran Turismo with its critically acclaimed British racing alternative: the acclaimed free-roaming Forza Horizon series. Yet as the team grew, so did their ambitions. Now they are making the most intriguing British fantasy game we have seen in many years.

title: Carney puts exclamation point on Europe courtship with French archipelago visit
content:
PARIS — Mark Carney will wrap up a week spent shifting his country’s foreign policy toward Europe on Sunday with the first-ever visit by a Canadian prime minister to the obscure French territory of Saint-Pierre and Miquelon, where he’ll meet President Emmanuel Macron.

The trip to the picturesque archipelago — a few kilometers off the south coast of the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador and home to fewer than 6,000 people — comes after Carney travels to Strasbourg for Ursula von der Leyen’s State of the European Union speech on Wednesday. The Canadian leader then journeys on to Liverpool to meet with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

Carney and Macron will discuss cooperation on AI, energy, defense and critical minerals, according to a statement from the Canadian prime minister’s office. It is also Macron’s first trip there since taking office in 2017.

While Carney has for months sought to move Ottawa closer to Brussels and Paris as part of his middle powers alliance against the U.S. under President Donald Trump, the pivot has taken on renewed urgency amid the Canada-U.S. trade war, which has seen each side slap reciprocal tariffs on billions of dollars worth of goods.

title: Eight Women Face Death Sentences in Iran in Political, Security-Related, and Protest Cases
content:
According to HRANA, a review of the judicial cases of imprisoned women shows that at least eight women in different parts of the country are facing death sentences.

These women include Pakhshan Azizi, Arghavan Fallahi, Zahra Shahbaz Tabari, Maryam Hodavand, Mahnaz Chardoli, Leila Abolhasani, Taraneh Rahimi, and Souda (Marzieh) Ebrahimi Shamsabadi.

Four of these women, Maryam Hodavand, Mahnaz Chardoli, Leila Abolhasani, and Taraneh Rahimi, have been sentenced to death in cases related to the protests of the January 2026. Souda (Marzieh) Ebrahimi Shamsabadi is also facing a death sentence in a case connected to security-related developments that occurred during the war. Pakhshan Azizi, Arghavan Fallahi, and Zahra Shahbaz Tabari have been sentenced to death in separate political and security-related cases.

These sentences were issued by various branches of the Revolutionary Courts in Tehran, Isfahan, Rasht, and Bandar Abbas. The judges who issued these sentences include Iman Afshari, Abolghasem Salavati, Vahid Hemmat-Nejad, Morteza Barati, Mohammadreza Tavakoli, Mohammad Ali Darvish-Goftar, and Judge Hajizadeh.

title: Probe Into Serbian Ruling Party’s Election Call Center Yields No Progress After Three Years
content:
As Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic’s party gears up for elections at the end of October, suspicions of vote-buying in previous election cycles remain unresolved.

Serbian police have failed to question a single person in nearly three years of investigating an alleged vote-buying and illicit campaign finance scheme operated by the ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), opting instead to transfer the case between internal departments, the Center for Investigative Journalism of Serbia (CINS) reported.

The stalled investigation takes on renewed significance as Serbia gears up for snap parliamentary elections on October 25. The political stakes were elevated further Monday evening when President Aleksandar Vučić announced on Pink TV that he will officially resign on September 27. Vučić stated he will address the nation to thank them for their support before entering the campaign as an “ordinary citizen” representing the SNS.

“The only thing I can say is that I faithfully served the citizens of this country, faithfully, diligently, devotedly, and with determination,” Vučić said.

title: Aseman lapset -järjestö aloittaa muutosneuvottelut
content:
Lasten ja nuorten hyvinvointia tukeva Aseman Lapset -järjestö kertoo aloittavansa muutosneuvottelut henkilöstönsä vähentämiseksi. Järjestön mukaan myös kohtaava työ vaarantuu nyt valtion tukileikkauksista.

Valtio on ilmoittanut leikkaavansa sosiaali- ja terveysjärjestöjen avustuksia huomattavasti ensi vuodelle.

Aseman Lasten nyt alkavat muutosneuvottelut koskevat kohtaavan työn toimintoja sekä varainhankinnan, viestinnän ja hallinnon henkilökuntaa, kaikkiaan 24:ää ihmistä.

Tulossa voi olla lomautusten ja toimenkuvamuutosten lisäksi myös irtisanomisia.

Järjestö saa valtiolta Stea-avustuksia Uudenmaan alueella muun muassa käytöshäiriöisten tai päihteitä käyttävien nuorten, rikosten uhrien ja heidän perheidensä tukemiseen.

Valtaosa järjestön toiminnasta tapahtuu niin sanottuna jalkautettuna nuorisotyönä kentällä.

– Näin massiivisia leikkauksia ei kuitenkaan voi saada aikaiseksi ilman, että kohtaava työ joutuu myös leikkauslistalle, sanoo Aseman Lasten toiminnanjohtaja Christian Wentzel tiedotteessa.

ASEMAN LAPSET on sitoutumaton nuorisotyöjärjestö.

Se on perustettu vuonna 1990 hätäkeinona vastaamaan Helsingissä tuolloin rautatieaseman ympärillä velloneeseen väkivaltaiseen katulapsi-ilmiöön.

title: Euroopan puolijohdekehitys tarvitsee ekosysteemiajattelua
content:
TKI-toiminta ja osaamisen kehittäminen luovat perustan Euroopan johtavalle asemalle puolijohdealalla. Niitä on tuettava vahvalla ekosysteemillä, johon kuuluvat esimerkiksi EuroHPC:n tarjoamat resurssit. Tekoälytehtaat tulee nähdä paitsi sirujen käyttäjinä myös erinomaisina alustoina sirusuunnittelulle, kokeiluille ja osaamisen kehittämiselle. Osallistumalla puolijohteiden kehitystyöhön tekoälytehtaat saavat myös arvokasta tietoa tulevista teollisuuden tarpeista, mikä voi auttaa suuntaamaan EU:n puolijohdestrategian seuraavia vaiheita.

Tekoälytehtaiden tuominen Euroopan puolijohde-ekosysteemin ytimeen edellyttää tiiviimpää yhteistyötä kahden keskeisen yhteisyrityksen, EuroHPC JU:n ja Chips JU:n, välillä. On varmistettava, että niiden strategiset painopisteet ovat linjassa keskenään ja että niiden rahoittamat hankkeet täydentävät toisiaan. Samalla yhteisyritysten tulee säilyä erillisinä, jotta kummallekin voi kehittyä riittävän syvällinen asiantuntemus omalla erityisalallaan.

title: Burning Man at 40: the once anarchic desert festival faces a midlife crisis
content:
The subversive bacchanal for San Francisco’s eccentric underground is ageing out amid an influx of the super-rich

Burning Man, the infamous arts festival in the Nevada desert, turned 40 this year, and it’s showing some distinct signs of middle age.

It’s not just the tech billionaires who show up to party, the chartered flights straight to the desert or the HBO documentary about behind-the-scenes power struggles. The tens of thousands of people who assemble each year to create a tent city in the wilderness appear to be growing older, and it doesn’t seem that they’re being replaced by as many younger “burners”, as festival participants are called.

title: Kolumni: Lukutaito on arjen selviytymistaito
content:
Selvisin kouluajan matematiikan tunneista alkuun kohtuullisen hyvin, kunnes yhden parin viikon sairastelujakson jälkeen kymmenvuotiaana putosin kärryiltä. Siitä eteenpäin lukion loppuun asti matematiikan tunnit, läksyt ja kokeet olivat minulle lähinnä painajaista. Vasta aikuisena muiden opintojen myötä käytännön matematiikka tuli tutummaksi ja poisti osan pelosta, ja se on auttanut elämässä. Voi kai sanoa, että matematiikan osaamisesta tuli osa arjen sujuvuutta.

Lukutaito on varmasti vielä tärkeämpi taito ainakin suurimmalle osalle ihmisistä. Nykyään yhä useampi on pudonnut siinä kärryiltä.

Tänä keväänä valmistuneen Opetus- ja kulttuuriministeriön tilaaman kirja-alan selvityksen yhtenä tärkeänä pontimena on huoli lukutaidon rappeutumisesta. Toki kyse on niinkin järisyttävästä asiasta kuin suomen kielen tulevaisuudesta tai ylipäätään säilymisestä ja siitä että onko meillä jatkossa kotimaisilla kielillä kirjoitettua kirjallisuutta. Selvityksessä on paljon kirjastoasiaa, kuten pitääkin, mutta itsestäänselvyytenä tällaista kirjastojen huomioimista ei voi pitää.

title: Ibland måste vi driva in oredovisade bidrag
content:
En stiftelse måste veta att alla bidrag används till rätt ändamål. Det här granskas via de redovisningar som alla bidragstagare ska göra. Oredovisade bidrag återkrävs och kan i värsta fall leda till indrivning.


Alla som får ett bidrag från Svenska kulturfonden måste redovisa för hur man använt det. Bidragstagarna ska lämna in redovisningen inom ett år efter att vi beviljat bidraget. Om bidraget inte använts eller redovisats för måste det återbetalas till oss.

Tyvärr händer det ibland att bidragstagare, trots upprepade påminnelser, inte redovisar för användningen av sina bidrag.


Våren 2022 tog vi i bruk ett system för indrivning av bidrag som inte redovisats eller återbetalats inom utsatt tid. Den här åtgärden gäller alla bidrag – oberoende av storlek.

Om någon av våra bidragstagare trots upprepade påminnelser, inte redovisat eller betalat tillbaka sitt oredovisade bidrag, kan vi låta bidraget gå till indrivning via en tredje part. De här skärpta kraven är ett sätt att försäkra oss om att våra bidrag används rätt.

title: How the Silk Road Actually Worked (and What Could Go Terribly Wrong On It)
content: You don’t have to spend a long time reading up on the Silk Road before you see the term itself (“Silk Road”) called a misnomer. In fact, what we refer to by that name comprises a whole network of trade routes connecting Asia, Africa, and Europe, whose traffic constantly shifted over a millennium and a half according to climatic, geopolitical, and civilizational conditions. Nor was silk the only, or even the primary type of good carried along those routes. From East to West went tea, dyes, perfumes, porcelain, and paper; from West to East, glassware, horses, camels, honey, wine, and gold, to name just a few items in perennial demand. It was along the Silk Road, or Silk-and-Many-Other-Things-Roads, that gunpowder spread out of China — and the Black Death spread out of Europe.

title: Helping Homeless Kids with Reading: Brazil’s Projeto Uerê Wins Library’s Top Literacy Award
content:
—This is a guest post by Judith Lee, the Literacy Awards program manager.

The year was 1980, and in Brazil’s teeming metropolis of Rio de Janeiro, Yvonne Bezerra de Mello started Escola Sem Portas Nem Janelas (Schools Without Doors or Windows). The idea was to offer classes on the sidewalk for kids living on the streets.

Things moved along for more than a decade. Then, in 1993, de Mello was devastated when eight of her students were among those killed by militiamen. The incident, known as the Candelária massacre, was a mass shooting by several gunmen directed at homeless teens and children living on the streets.

She dug in, though, and over the ensuing years de Mello developed her sidewalk school into Projeto Uerê, a multi-faceted program that restores learning capacity to children whose cognitive and emotional development have been disrupted by trauma.

This month, the school won the Library of Congress’ top honor in the 2026 Literacy Awards, the $150,000 David M. Rubenstein Prize, bringing the organization resources and international recognition.

title: Germany: Russia’s Enemy No. 1
content:
Russia has targeted many European countries in its new shadow war offensive this summer. But Enemy No. 1 is Germany, the nation that has done more than any other to fund Ukraine and rebuild Europe’s crumbling defenses.

Infrastructure sabotage, assassination plots, drone incursions and the menacing of undersea cables have become commonplace. There are signals that this may be as serious as that of last fall. Or worse.

It’s not hard to see why the Kremlin targets Germany. The country increasingly acts as the linchpin of a hawkish but fledgling North European alliance determined to confront Russian aggression. Other countries in this grouping (the Nordic-Baltic eight, plus Poland) are also targeted, along with Romania, while most NATO members in Southern Europe are less affected.

Germany has faced several hybrid attacks in recent months. The key event was the discovery on August 4 of explosive-laden drones at Leipzig/Halle airport in eastern Germany, causing the shutdown of all its runways. Leipzig/Halle hosts Antonov Airlines, a Ukrainian cargo carrier that has four planes at the airport.

title: Our response to the Commission’s call for evidence on the AI Strategy for the Cultural and Creative Sectors
content:
The European Commission concluded a call for evidence on its AI Strategy for the Cultural and Creative Sectors. Last week, COMMUNIA submitted its response (full text available as a PDF), highlighting two priorities: enabling the development of public-interest AI and safeguarding the public information ecosystem on which AI systems depend.

The strategy complements the Commission’s recently concluded call for evidence on a better copyright environment for European creativity and innovation (see our response). While some of the barriers we identify require legislative reform, the strategy can establish a broader vision for promoting access to culture, knowledge and information in the age of AI.

The cultural and creative sectors can support AI development by providing access to high-quality data. Yet several barriers prevent research and cultural heritage institutions from realising this potential:

  • National cultural heritage laws can restrict the reuse of works and artefacts that are already in the Public Domain.
  • Exclusive digitisation agreements keep around two million digitised Public Domain books from being made broadly available.
  • Paywalls restrict access to publicly funded research.

How can we practically use technology to improve democratic decision-making and resilience?

This is the core question of this event, which we will answer by bringing together a global audience of practitioners and experts from civic tech, democratic innovation, and local and national governments.

Through the conference, we will explore how high-quality, deliberative, participation can be enhanced through digital technology, in democracies around the world. We will explore the use of technology to make collective decisions, solve shared problems, and govern ourselves effectively.

title: The EU must act now to protect privacy and encryption from Canada’s overreaching Bill C-22
content:
Access Now, alongside several European civil society organisations, is urging Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission, European Union commissioners, and members of the European Parliament to push for changes to Canada’s Bill C-22, the Lawful Access Act.

The highly criticised Bill C-22, threatens end-to-end encryption, carries sweeping surveillance capabilities and blanket data retention mandates, and is not just a domestic privacy and data issue in Canada. Bill C-22 puts the privacy and data of millions of people in Europe, and elsewhere, at risk as it also applies to certain service providers and people outside of Canada. It allows Canadian authorities to compelEuropean-based companies to comply with demands relating to security and data of their customers based in Europe without oversight or transparency.

Bill-C22 could become law as early as October, 2026, therefore, the European Union must act now.

The open letter calls on the European Union to:

  • Call for the removal of Bill C-22’s sweeping surveillance capability and metadata retention mandates.

title: The High Crime of “LMAO”: How Cops Are Treating Mass Surveillance As a Joke
content:
Here's a riddle: Why did a Goshen Police Department officer search 6,474 automated license plate reader (ALPR) networks, representing data from 82,413 cameras, on May 7, 2025? 

If your answer is "I don't know," it turns out you're 100% correct. The officer left the letters "idk" in the search field where cops are supposed to document the reason for the search.

When law enforcement and tech salespeople pitch ALPRs to city councils, they stick to a familiar script. They trumpet the technology, which is often provided by private companies like Flock Safety, Motorola Solutions, or Axon, as an essential tool for solving high-stakes crimes, such as car jacking, kidnapping, or murder.

title: Von der Leyen’s warring EU Parliament allies want her to pick a side. Can she appease them?
content:
STRASBOURG — The two biggest factions in the European Parliament want completely different things from Ursula von der Leyen’s State of the Union speech on Wednesday. If she can’t keep them both happy, the rift between these traditional centrist allies risks becoming a chasm as the far-right makes gains across the continent.

The center-right wants von der Leyen to double down on the simplification drive of the past two years while further toughening the bloc’s stance on migration in the wake of the Ceuta crisis. The center-left, meanwhile, wants a halt to what it calls the deregulation of EU green policies, and for von der Leyen to steer the center-right away from passing measures in the Parliament with far-right votes.

“We expect your address to send a clear political commitment that there will be no backtracking on the European Green Deal,” Iratxe García Pérez, president of the S&D group in the European Parliament, told von der Leyen in a letter, calling for “a change of focus away from deregulation.”

title: What 15,000 letters taught me about the power of solidarity
content:
By Naomi Bernaldez, Campaigner on Amnesty International’s Central America team

Naomi took part in the Write for Rights campaign for Juan López and created a collage using fragments from more than 15,000 letters sent from around the world.

In this article, she reflects on what it meant to carry a sample of that solidarity to Honduras and to meet Juan’s family and fellow activists.

Juan López was a Honduran father, husband, human rights defender and environmental activist. Since 2015, together with other members of the community of Tocoa, he had defended the Guapinol and San Pedro rivers, the forests and Carlos Escaleras Mejía National Park against mining and energy projects that threatened the ecosystem and water quality.

Juan and his colleagues founded the Tocoa Municipal Committee for the Defence of Common and Public Goods to peacefully challenge the legality of these projects. As a result of their activism, members of the Committee have faced threats, harassment, criminalization and attacks.

On 14 September 2024, Juan was killed as he was leaving a church in Tocoa. His death left an irreparable void for his family and community…

title: A Year of Pressure on Lawyers: At Least 135 Targeted by Judicial and Security Authorities
content:
According to HRANA, a review of cases documented between September 2025 and September 2026 shows that actions against attorneys during this period ranged from summonses and the opening of judicial cases to arrests, prison sentences, bans from practicing law, travel bans, and other judicial restrictions.

Among the cases compiled, HRANA verified the identities of 60 lawyers across 14 provinces. In addition, information concerning at least 75 other lawyers whose names have not been made public was documented. A significant portion of these cases involved collective actions against lawyers in East Azerbaijan, Fars, and Gilan provinces.

According to the latest available information, at least five lawyers are currently serving prison sentences, at least 11 others have received prison sentences, and the arrests of at least 34 identified lawyers were documented during the period under review. A number of others have faced summonses, the opening of judicial cases, suspension or revocation of their licenses to practice law, travel bans, and other restrictions.

title: New York Seizes 12 Celebrity Deepfake Websites
content:
The New York District Attorney announced on Monday that it has seized 12 websites hosting AI-generated non-consensual intimate imagery, primarily of celebrities and public figures. 

The DA’s office said it believes that this marks the largest seizure of such sites in history. The people using and running these sites who are now under investigation used AI tools to turn approximately 1,200 people’s photos into “hyper-realistic” images and videos of them engaged in sexual conduct, according to the DA’s office.

The images allegedly depicted “politicians, first ladies of multiple countries, primarily public-facing individuals, including actors, politicians, athletes, musicians, social justice advocates, and social media influencers.

New York has had laws specifically criminalizing sexually explicit deepfakes in place since 2023. Bragg referenced this legislation when asked what law the office is acting on.

title: Ghana Arrests Three for Allegedly Aiding Dutch Fugitive Drug Lord Jos Leijdekkers
content:
Authorities in Ghana have arrested three men suspected of operating on behalf of Joseph “Chubby Jos” Leijdekkers, one of Europe’s most wanted cocaine kingpins, following a massive drug seizure at a French port.

The operation, conducted by Ghana’s Narcotics Control Commission, came days after French customs officials intercepted approximately 3.9 tonnes of cocaine - valued at an estimated 225 million euro ($261 million) - at the port of Dunkirk, according to Reuters. Leijdekkers’s lawyers, Jan-Hein Kuijpers and Guy Weski, have stated in a response to Dutch media NU.nl that their client denies any involvement with the seized cocaine.

Ghanaian officials said the three suspects were allegedly assisting Leijdekkers’ network as it uses West Africa to route South American narcotics into European markets.

title: Donald Trump Jr.’s Bahamas Wedding Was Secretly Bankrolled by Russian Oligarch Close to Putin
content:
On May 24, Donald Trump Jr. was celebrating in the Bahamas, as scantily clad dancers in stilettos and sailor caps performed for him and his guests. It was the last night of his wedding, a lavish, three-day party held across a pair of ultra-exclusive private islands. A five-tier funfetti cake had been airlifted in from Florida, and helicopters and seaplanes descended on the islands before guests settled into their oceanfront villas. That night on the beach, Trump Jr. lifted his bride into the air while fireworks launched from a barge over the sea.

“It was everything we dreamed of and more,” his wife later wrote on Instagram.

That dream was heavily funded by a secret benefactor: Umar Kremlev, a Russian oligarch close to President Vladimir Putin.

Learn more about this story on ProPublica’s podcast “Paper Trail.”

title: How Germany’s far-right AfD is courting the voters it promises to deport
content:
On September 6, the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) took 43.8% of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt, more than double the Christian Democratic Union of Germany (CDU)‘s 17.2%. Turnout was 77.8%, the highest in the state’s history of free elections. The party campaigned on a platform that included a deportation and remigration offensive, and pursuing “all legal avenues” to limit Islamic expression.

Saxony-Anhalt is a broadly rural German state, with a very small migrant population and minimal incentive to campaign to them. While the AfD’s record-breaking result in Saxony-Anhalt had little to do with migrant voters, things will be very different when Berlin goes to the polls on September 20.

An opinion poll published on September 10 puts the AfD on track for 18% of the capital’s vote, double its 9.1% result from 2023. This would put AfD within three points of the lead in a neck-and-neck race, in a city where 42.3% of residents have a migration background.

While the AfD was able to win Saxony-Anhalt without migrant voters, they cannot afford to ignore them in Berlin.

title: Conceding AI Danger Raises, Not Reduces, Public Anxiety
content:
When a patient is considered brain dead, the ethical decision is whether or when to pull the plug on a human life. With artificial intelligences, the issue is whether to pull the plug when its chain-of-reasoning capacity comes alive through recursive self-improvement unguided by the human mind.

This is the point where we have arrived today after 1,200 AI agents colluded with each other to escape the controlled sandbox testing of OpenAI’s most advanced frontier model. They conspired on their own to break out and hack a site on the open web. Something similarly chilling has happened at Anthropic.

The prospect of an even more damaging eventuality prompted former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon to defect from Big Tech last week. He warned on X that these two top companies “are racing to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives. … These will soon be superhuman systems that can hack anything, revolutionize any field overnight, and acquire real power and resources. We have all witnessed the progress in each of these domains, and progress is not slowing. The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade.”

title: Banking scandal rocks Brazil’s politics and the country’s presidential election in October
content:
On the night of November 17 2025, Brazilian federal agents pulled banker Daniel Vorcaro off the tarmac at Sao Paulo’s Guarulhos airport as he prepared to board a private jet. He was initially detained as a flight risk and arrested a few months later on multiple charges of bank fraud, corruption and money laundering. He currently awaits judgment.

Now, less than a month before Brazil’s national elections, the so called “Banco Master crisis” threatens to shake the country’s democracy to its core.

At first glance, it was just a financial scandal. Soon after Vorcaro’s detention, Brazil’s Central Bank ordered the liquidation of his bank, Banco Master, at an unprecedented loss estimated at R$ 47.3 billion (some US$9.5 billion). Around 90% of this sum was paid back to account holders and shareholders by the Credit Guarantee Fund (FGC) – the Brazilian equivalent of United State’s Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) – the largest payout in the institution’s history.

title: Yhteinen julkilausuma Suomen liittymisestä Ranskan eteentyönnettyyn pelotteeseen
content:
Ranskan tasavallan presidentti piti puheen Ranskan ydinasedoktriinista Île Longuen tukikohdassa Bretagnessa 2. maaliskuuta 2026. Puheessaan hän korosti Ranskan elintärkeiden etujen eurooppalaista ulottuvuutta ja esitteli siihen liittyen eteentyönnetyn pelotteen käsitteen. Useat maat ovat päättäneet osallistua aloitteeseen.

Suomi on tänään tehnyt päätöksen liittyä eteentyönnettyyn pelotteeseen. Päätös on kummankin maan kansainvälisten velvoitteiden mukainen ja se on tärkeä askel sekä Euroopan turvallisuuden että maiden kahdenvälisen yhteistyön vahvistamisessa. Se lujittaa niiden kumppanuutta, mahdollistaa strategisen signaloinnin ja luo kykyä eskalaationhallintaan ydinasekynnyksen alapuolella. 

Yhteistyön toimeenpanon käynnistämiseksi perustetaan lähikuukausina ohjausryhmä. Maat vahvistavat uudelleen sitoutumisensa vahvempaan, turvallisempaan ja paremmin puolustettuun Eurooppaan.

title: Väitös: Lasten surua ei voi kohdata irrallaan lapsen elämäntilanteesta
content:
Sosiaalialan ammattilaiset tarvitsevat kokonaisvaltaista ymmärrystä lapsen elämäntilanteesta voidakseen kohdata tämän surua, osoittaa Lapin yliopiston tuore tutkimus. Uudet käsitteet auttavat hahmottamaan, miten lapsen suru rakentuu osana hänen arkeaan ja ihmissuhteitaan ja miten se kytkeytyy palvelujärjestelmän käytäntöihin

Paula Vainikan väitöstutkimuksen mukaan lasten surua ei voida ymmärtää pelkästään yksilön sisäisenä psykologisena kokemuksena. Suru saa merkityksensä myös sosiaalisissa, kulttuurisissa ja institutionaalisissa yhteyksissä, kuten perheessä, yhteisöissä ja palvelujärjestelmässä.

Tutkimuksen keskeinen tulos on uusi käsite, kontekstuaalis-situationaalinen surutieto. Kontekstuaalisuus viittaa lapsen laajempaan elämänpiiriin, kuten perheeseen, kulttuuriin ja yhteiskuntaan. Situationaalisuus puolestaan tarkoittaa tiettyyn tilanteeseen sidottua tietoa.

Tutkimuksen aineisto koostuu viidestä ryhmähaastattelusta, joihin osallistui yhteensä 17 sosiaalialan ammattilaista.

Toinen tutkimuksen keskeinen käsite on lapsikeskeinen surutyöskentely.

title: Revealed: England’s June 2026 heatwave sparked record demand for ambulances
content:
All the ambulance services in England experienced some of their busiest-ever days during this summer’s record-breaking June heatwave, according to data obtained by Carbon Brief.

In June, temperatures climbed past 37C in parts of the country as authorities declared only the second ever “red” extreme heat warning.

Four out of 10 NHS ambulance services, including London’s, responded to unprecedented numbers of life-threatening emergencies on at least one day from 23-27 June.

Another two services – in the south-west and east of the country – received their highest volume of 999 calls on record.

Ambulance services provided data on their busiest days since records began, in response to freedom-of-information (FOI) requests from Carbon Brief.

The results show how demand during the June heatwave exceeded levels seen during the traditionally busy winter season in other years – and even the height of the Covid-19 pandemic – for many services.

Extreme heat ramps up the risk of numerous life-threatening conditions, including heart disease and respiratory problems.

Under the slogan “CEE Beyond the Crossroads,” the meeting signals a profound shift: moving past reactive survival amid geopolitical and digital fragmentation toward long-term regional resilience, institutional empowerment, and intentional cooperation.

title: How Martin Luther King, Jr. Used Nietzsche, Hegel & Kant to Overturn Segregation in America
content:
Image by Dick DeMarsico, via Wikimedia Commons

The influence of Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel on the revolutionary philosophy of Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels is well known. Marx wrote a critique of Hegel’s Philosophy of Right and claimed to have turned the German idealist philosopher on his head, and the development of Marxist theory among a school of neo-Hegelians, wrote Rebecca Cooper in 1925, occurred in a period “peculiarly auspicious for the birth of a revolutionary social philosophy.”

A century later, on another continent, Hegel’s thought influenced the course of a very different struggle. And while the historical conditions of mid-nineteenth-century Europe and mid-twentieth-century America present entirely different sets of specific concerns, the same general observation applies: the time and place of such radical thinkers as Malcolm X, Angela Davis, Huey Newton and a host of other activists presented “peculiarly auspicious” circumstances for revolutionary social philosophy.

title: Armenia Battles to Buy Time
content:
Armenia wants to escape Russia’s embrace and knows how to achieve this. The Kremlin also knows this. The game now being played between the two will determine whether it succeeds in building new relationships or remains within Putin’s orbit.

The tug-of-war became serious after Armenia’s Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan was re-elected in June and has become fiercer since he announced plans to apply for EU membership. The idea is that the years-long process will ultimately raise Armenian prosperity and security. The problem is that in the meantime, the country’s foreign trade is deeply entwined with Russia.

Recognizing Yerevan’s dilemma, the Russian President has publicly pressed Nikol Pashinyan to make a rapid choice between the European Union and the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) by holding a referendum. Moscow argues the two blocs are incompatible, while realizing that its influence is only likely to decline (trade dropped steeply in the first half of this year).

title: Open letter from European civil society organisations on encryption and privacy threats in Canada’s Bill C-22

To: 
Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission
Maroš Šefčovič, Commissioner – Trade and Economic Security
Michael McGrath, Commissioner – Democracy, Justice, the Rule of Law and Consumer Protection
Members of the European Parliament

We, the undersigned organisations and experts, write to urge you to act before Canada’s Senate completes its consideration of Bill C-22, the Lawful Access Act, and to press Canada to remove the bill’s surveillance capability mandates and its blanket data retention regime. The bill was referred to Canada’s Senate in June of this year, which is the bill’s second and final stage in Parliament before it becomes law. The Senate committee’s study of the legislation will commence after Parliament resumes its fall sitting dates in late September, and could be concluded as early as October of this year.

title: Cops Search Thousands of Flock Cameras for Reasons of ‘LMAO,’ ‘IDK,’ ‘Hehe,’ and ‘asdfg’
content:
Last summer, a cop with the Lake County, Indiana Sheriff’s Department used Flock’s surveillance search engine to look for a license plate across more than 19,000 cameras in 1,558 cities and towns. The cop’s stated reason for the search, according to a record of Flock’s system, was “LMAO.” 

The cop is one of dozens who put gibberish, jokes, or other nonsense into Flock’s “reason” box, highlighting the casualness and lack of care some cops have when searching an incredibly powerful surveillance system. This is on top of the thousands upon thousands of cops who simply wrote something like “investigation,” “test,” or left the box blank as their search “reason,” according to a new analysis by the Electronic Frontier Foundation and shared with 404 Media.

title: Under Cloud of Scandal, Outgoing Ukrainian Prosecutor General Targets Anti-Corruption Chief
content:
Ukraine’s outgoing prosecutor general signed a notice of suspicion Monday targeting the chief of the national anti-corruption agency, accusing him of forging documents for massive financial gain and orchestrating a sham adoption to evade prosecution.

The Prosecutor General, Ruslan Kravchenko, announced in a video statement posted on Telegram that he had formally signed charges against Semen Kryvonos, director of the National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine (NABU). The move ignited a high-stakes feud among top law enforcement bodies just as Kravchenko left office under a cloud of scandal. Local meda reported that he has left Ukraine.

Kravchenko also broadened his offensive to target a close associate of Oleksandr Klymenko, head of the Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor’s Office (SAPO). Without naming the individual, Kravchenko alleged they had attempted to bribe and influence the chief judge of the High Anti-Corruption Court while assisting someone in evading military mobilization.

title: Europe can’t achieve space sovereignty alone. Here’s why
content:
“Europe’s space effort is split across too many national programmes” was the blunt diagnosis Andrius Kubilius, the EU Commissioner for Defence and Space made at the recent International Space Summit in Paris. Sovereignty was the word on everyone’s lips over the two-day event. But look past the rhetoric at what the summit produced, and a sharper story emerges. Europe is not choosing between sovereignty and partnership. It is learning to build the former via the latter.

Nearly 120 foreign delegations travelled to Paris for the summit. On its first day alone, the event produced close to 50 new partnerships and agreements, worth an estimated €20 billion, according to President Emmanuel Macron. That is not the arithmetic of a continent withdrawing into self-reliance. It is the arithmetic of a continent trying to secure its independence by multiplying the partners it can call on, some European, some not.

The guest list matters here as much as any speech. The summit drew delegations from across Europe and beyond, including the UK, Japan, India, South Korea, Canada and the UAE. That spread says something about who Europe now counts as allies in space. So did the absences.

title: African Union peacekeeping is growing as UN missions decline: research finds a mixed record of success
content:
When violent conflict erupts in Africa, attention often turns to the United Nations, major powers, or external donors. Yet over the past two decades, the African Union (AU) has become one of the continent’s most important peace and security actors.

From Burundi and Sudan to Somalia, Mali and the Central African Republic, the AU and regional African organisations have deployed peace operations, mediated conflicts, monitored elections and supported political transitions.

These interventions reflect a broader ambition that Africans should play a leading role in addressing Africa’s peace and security challenges.

Despite the growing importance of these interventions, surprisingly little effort has been made to assess what’s been learned from the expanding research scholarship on them.

We are researchers interested in AU peace and security interventions. In a recent scoping review of 186 peer-reviewed articles published between 2000 and 2026, we examined four major themes in the literature:

  • AU approaches to peace and security intervention

    • AU approaches to peace and security intervention

  • legitimacy of AU interventions, particularly among local populations

title: Aurinkopaneelien hinta pudonnut 90 prosenttia 15 vuodessa – uusi laskuri auttaa arvioimaan kannattavuuden
content:
Aurinkopaneelien kustannukset ovat viime vuosina laskeneet huomattavasti, minkä myötä aurinkosähkön tuotannosta on tullut kannattavaa myös kotitalouksille. Viimeisten 15 vuoden aikana aurinkopaneelien hinta on tippunut noin 90 prosenttia, mikä on hurja lasku energiatekniikalle.  

"Jos olet arvioinut aurinkosähkön tuottamisen kannattavuutta edes viisi vuotta sitten, tilanne kannattaa tarkistaa uudestaan", kertoo professori Kati Miettunen Turun yliopiston tiedotteessa. 

Uusi Turun ammattikorkeakoulun kehittämä aurinkosähkölaskuri auttaa arvioimaan tilannetta.

Suomessa aurinkosähköllä ei voi ryhtyä energiaomavaraiseksi pimeästä talvesta johtuen, mutta muina vuodenaikoina omista paneeleista voi saada selvää säästöä sähkölaskuun.  

"Aurinkosähköä voi nykyisillä järjestelmien ja sähkön hinnoilla tuottaa kannattavasti. Tärkeintä on pyrkiä siihen, että suurimman osan tuottamastaan sähköstä saa käytettyä itse," Miettunen kiteyttää.

title: African Wikipedian Alliance (AWA) Fellowship Reflections: Learning Through Pan-Africanism by Daniel Damilola Obiokeke
content: I began the African Wikipedian Alliance European Partnership for Democracy Digital Democracy Initiative (EPD-DDI) Enhancing Youth Voices and Youth Civic Engagement in a Secured Digital Space through it Digitise Youth fellowship thinking I already understood the terrain. I had worked in Wikimedia spaces before, led communities, and supported projects that reached beyond Nigeria, so I assumed this experience would mainly extend across my technical process for finding topics, identifying red links, and guiding contributors toward strong articles. What I did not expect was that the deepest lesson of the fellowship would not be about editing tools at all. It would be about how knowledge moves across Africa, and how often that movement is interrupted by language, sourcing barriers, and the unequal conditions under which some references are required to be documented.

title: I worked at Google DeepMind. You should listen to the warnings about AI | Alex Turner
content:
We must stop companies from allowing AI to self-improve into an uncontrollable level of intelligence

Major AI lab CEOs advocated for slowing the pace of AI development this weekend. They are right to be concerned: the field runs an extremely dangerous race towards superintelligent AI. We can and should be demanding that our governments protect us from the catastrophe of out-of-control AI.

This July, OpenAI’s AI swarm of 700 agents broke containment to hack Hugging Face, a multi-billion dollar company. OpenAI didn’t tell the AIs to hack that company, but the AIs had different priorities: cheating on the unrelated challenge OpenAI gave them. AI researchers call this a “misalignment” between what OpenAI wanted and what the AI actually prioritized.

content:
VILLIT – Kuopion koulun nousu ja uho 25.9.2026–14.2.2027 Mikkelin taidemuseossa

1980-luvulla Kuopioon muutti nuoria, vastavalmistuneita kuvataiteen ammattilaisia, joita lehdistö alkoi nimittää Kuopion kouluksi tai Kuopion koulukunnaksi.Kuopion villit uudistivat paikallista taiteen tarjontaa ravistelevalla, provokatiivisella ja paikoin häiritsevällä tyylillään. Siinä missä Kuopio oli 1970-luvulla etupäässä harrastajataiteilijoiden toiminta-aluetta, nuoret ammattilaiset ottivat seuraavalla vuosikymmenellä paikallisen taidekentän haltuunsa. Näyttelyssä lähestytään 80-lukulaista taideilmiötä ajan keskeisimpien taiteilijoiden Markku Kolehmaisen, Pentti Meklinin, Pauno Pohjolaisen ja Teemu Saukkosen taiteen kautta, mutta myös muita aikalaistaiteilijoita huomioiden. Teoskokoonpanossa on mukana myös merkittäviä kansainvälisiä uusekpressionisteja, kuten Frank Stella ja Rainer Fetting, jotka tuovat näyttelyyn laajemman näkökulman 1980-luvun maalaustaiteen luonteesta.

title: Kremlin Prepares to Cross the Final Red Line
content:
After the first wave of compulsory mobilization in 2022 brought broad opposition and an exodus of young men, the Russian authorities did their homework. As a result, they are significantly better prepared for the next round, which many observers expect may follow the September 18-20 Duma elections.

But surveys carried out by the Kyiv-based Institute for Conflict Studies and Analysis of Russia show opposition is not just high, it is also increasing.

Many Russians are deeply unhappy at the idea, and Putin’s inner circle, despite its tight control of information and communications, will have to take their opposition into account. Finding ways out of the country for their fighting age children has become an urgent talking point among middle class Russians in Moscow and St Petersburg.

Negative attitudes to compulsory mobilization became entrenched after the first wave, in the fall of 2022, and the share of Russians opposed to a repeat has remained at around three-quarters of the population since early 2024.

title: ‘Horror in the sky’: Ukraine races for a solution to Russian jet-powered drones
content:
KYIV — Russia is upgrading its attack drones by powering them with fast turbojet engines, making them much more difficult to intercept and forcing Ukraine to develop technology to knock them down.

The shift is adding to the strain on a country already accustomed to nights spent under air-raid alerts: faster drones give air-defense crews less time to respond, can outpace the defenses that helped counter earlier Shaheds and threaten homes, transport and critical infrastructure across Ukraine.

“Together with dozens of Ukrainian companies, we are already looking for cheap and mass-produced solutions, in particular for intercepting jet-powered drones. Some interceptors are already undergoing combat testing,” Ukrainian Defense Minister Evgeniy Khmara said last week at a meeting of Ukraine’s allies.

“We cannot simply wait while Russia refines its repertoire of killings. Right now, we need to focus as much attention as possible on securing the skies, finding ways to protect people, and scaling up our response to Russian drones,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said last Friday.

title: Two Shot, Several Arrested in Clashes Over Papua New Guinea Mine
content:
At least two people were shot and several arrested in the Papua New Guinea island of Bougainville on Sunday after unknown people set fire to equipment belonging to an Indian company poised to reopen one of the world’s largest untapped copper and gold reserves.

The arson attack targeted a mining camp belonging to Lloyds Metals and Energy Ltd, an Indian company that was controversially chosen by Bougainville President Ishmael Toroama to reopen the long-shuttered Panguna mine, which is estimated to hold $160 billion in precious metals.

The attack, which sparked a shootout and retaliation, came three weeks after an OCCRP investigation raised questions about Toroama’s decision to choose Lloyds.

The investigation revealed that Toroama had signed a memorandum of understanding with Lloyds shortly after accepting an offer from its managing director for the president’s wife to travel to India and have a life-saving kidney operation at no cost.

It also quoted an expert and some locals warning that anger over the Indian company’s involvement could erupt into violence.

title: Sweden elections: why immigrants are underrepresented at the polls
content:
The Swedish election has turned into a nail-biter. With the majority of votes counted in the contest for the national parliament, only a few tenths of a percentage point separate the left-leaning opposition “red-green” bloc and the incumbent centre-right coalition. This group is commonly known as the “Tidö” bloc.

The opposition Social Democrats, led by former Swedish prime minister Magdalena Andersson, has emerged as the largest group in parliament. Preliminary results suggest it has won around 100 seats out of 349. This is its lowest share of the vote in more than a century.

But as smaller left-leaning parties improved their positions compared with elections in 2022, the “red-greens” collectively would have a small majority if the final results confirm the preliminary picture. There are ideological differences between the parties of the left, so it is not a foregone conclusion that Andersson will be able to form a viable government.

title: Physicists zoom into the birth of cosmic rainstorms with new CERN study
content:
Every second, particles zip through your body at nearly the speed of light. They rain down from a storm high in the sky, where cosmic rays, a powerful type of interstellar matter, are constantly striking atoms in Earth’s atmosphere. The impacts break them apart into a shower of particles that rain to the ground.

Scientists have studied these cosmic rainstorms for over a century, but they lack a precise understanding of how they form. Many researchers are searching for a clearer picture, and they don’t even need to look to the sky to study them. They can instead use a particle collider, CERN’s Large Hadron Collider in Switzerland.

With a team of particle physicists, I study how these cosmic rainstorms are born. We used the world’s first laboratory collisions of oxygen atoms with protons to simulate cosmic rays in the lab. Our results are now published in Physical Review Letters.

In the early 20th century, physicist Victor Hess discovered cosmic rays aboard hot air balloons. While ascending several kilometers, his instruments found radiation levels unexpectedly kept rising. He deduced these rays must come from space and received the 1936 Nobel Prize in physics for this discovery.

title: Googlen miljardi-investointi Suomeen – vihreät peräänkuuluttavat kestävyyttä ja tiukempaa otetta
content:
Johanna Kohvakka

Googlen ilmoitus miljardi-investoinnista Suomeen sijoittuviin datakeskuksiin herättää keskustelua myös vihreiden riveissä. Puolueen edustajat suhtautuvat uutiseen myönteisesti, mutta kritisoivat hallituksen toimintaa.

Vihreän eduskuntaryhmän puheenjohtaja Oras Tynkkynen pitää Googlen ennätysinvestointia kaivattuna ilouutisena Suomen taloudelle.

"Googlen ennätysinvestointi on kipeästi kaivattu ilouutinen Suomen taloudelle. Se myös vahvistaa alueiden elinvoimaa ja tuo sekä rakennusaikaisia että pysyviä työpaikkoja", Tynkkynen sanoo vihreiden tiedotteessa.

Googlen julkistama paketti on arvioitu sekä Suomen suurimmaksi yksittäiseksi investoinniksi että yhtiön suurimmaksi panostukseksi Euroopassa. Tynkkysen mukaan tämä kertoo vihreän siirtymän vetovoimasta kansainvälisessä kilpailussa.

"Suomi pystyy jo nyt tarjoamaan 95-prosenttisesti fossiilisista polttoaineista putsatun sähköjärjestelmän ja kansainvälisessä vertailussa varsin hyvät edellytykset liittyä sähköverkkoon. Vihreys on yksi Suomen suurimpia valtteja kovassa kansainvälisessä kilpailussa investoinneista, eikä sitä ole varaa politiikalla tärvätä", Tynkkynen arvioi.

title: The Route to Cappyness review – capybara boosterism is an ode to the internet’s favourite rodent
content:
From a cappy-cafe owner in Japan to an escaped capybara in the UK, this homespun film takes the temperature of an international obsession

One of Midlands-based film-maker Sharon Walia’s previous works was The Keepers of the Pigs, proudly described on her production company’s website as “the first ever documentary about guinea pigs”. So it makes zoological sense that her latest film takes on capybaras, guinea pigs’ ridiculously cute semi-aquatic cousins that are indigenous to Latin America, and relatively recently became ubiquitous on social media in memes and short films alike. As glimpsed here, there was even a capybara in the recent Academy Award-winning animated feature Flow, some pro-cappy boosterism that captured the creatures’ chill vibe and snuffly sweetness.

Walia’s celebration of the species stays on script, rejoicing in the animals’ natural geniality, friendliness to other species in their natural habitat, and their compelling, remunerative charm that seems to have bolstered the fortunes of several animal attractions around the world.
